system_time_api: System.DateTime.UtcNow.ToFileTimeUtc, read at the instant it changes value; its resolution is the system timer increment, 0.5 to 15 ms per https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.datetime.utcnow; GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime is not reachable from Windows PowerShell 5.1 without compiling code
time_adjustment_api: GetSystemTimeAdjustment is not called (same reason); both members of time_adjustment are null in the manifest
samples_file: samples.jsonl, one JSON object per pair, in the order taken; a decoder cites line:<n>; edge says whether the pair was taken at a change of the system clock, step_100ns is the size of that change
method: one thread reads Stopwatch.GetTimestamp (QueryPerformanceCounter), [DateTime]::UtcNow.ToFileTimeUtc() (the system time at the resolution of the system timer), Stopwatch.GetTimestamp, at the session start, every 5 s strictly inside the session, and at the stop. Each pair is taken at the instant the system clock changes value: the clock is read in a loop until it changes, and the counter read before the last unchanged reading and the one after the changed reading bracket the moment the clock took its new value; the size of that change (the clock increment) is recorded with the pair. The frequency is Stopwatch.Frequency (QueryPerformanceFrequency). GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime and GetSystemTimeAdjustment are not called: neither is reachable from Windows PowerShell 5.1 without compiling code, so both members of time_adjustment are null. See docs/clock-calibration.md.
